chunk_findings.detail: `_sh_c` returns the index of the `-c` word and `_commands` always takes `head[i + 1]` as the shell program. Bash reads the program from the first non-option argument after option parsing, and option arguments are not that word. `bash -co pipefail 'git push origin main'` runs `git push` (`c` is `-c`, `pipefail` is the `-o` optarg), but `last` stays on `-co` and the inspected string is `pipefail`, so `check` returns None. The same miss happens for `bash -c -x 'git push origin main'` (payload taken is `-x`) and `bash -c -- 'git push origin main'` / `bash -c - 'git push origin main'` (payload taken is `--` or `-`; a lone `-` is end-of-options, which this loop skips and continues past). A `c` in a `+` cluster is also treated as `-c`, so `bash +c 'git push origin main'` is refused even though that word is a script name, not a `-c` program.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_sh_c

data.probe: confirmed and fixed in c6f629c79: _sh_c now scans option words first and returns the FIRST non-option argument as the -c run string, so 'bash -c -x/--/-' and 'bash -co pipefail <cmd>' are all refused (regression added to test_refused_clustered_c_flag; 111 tests pass). The '+c' sub-claim is empirically wrong: bash +c 'echo X' DOES run echo, so refusing it is correct, not a false positive.
